solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fungus in ground you reported

indicators.note: reported means said out loud, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: ground is the past tense of grind, as corn is milled; you is written U in text speak and sounds the same

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a fungus was found in the soil you mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like soil, but it is the past tense of grind: MILLED. 'reported' signals that MILLED YOU spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mildew is a thin whitish growth of mould, a kind of fungus on plants and damp surfaces.

clue.text: Male worker criticises mischievous females

parts.note: an ant is the standard worker insect
raps means criticises sharply

explanation.surface: A man at work complains about troublesome women.
explanation.definitionFit: Mantrap is an old word for a woman thought to ensnare men, so a flirtatious seductress.

clue.text: House that has a Victorian pavilion

definitions.meaning: the House of ..., upper chamber of the UK Parliament
... is the London cricket ground, whose pavilion dates from 1890

explanation.surface: A building with a nineteenth-century pavilion attached.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lords is Parliament's upper house, and Lord's cricket ground is famous for its Victorian pavilion.

clue.text: What would be found in alphabet hitherto

definitions.text: What would be found in alphabet hitherto

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A question about what once belonged in the alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: eth was a letter of the Old English alphabet, no longer used.
explanation.definitionFit: Eth is a letter, written as a crossed d, used in Old English for a th sound.

clue.text: Worked in a forest and made slow plodding progress?

definitions.meaning: to lumber is to fell and prepare timber
to lumber is also to move heavily and clumsily

explanation.surface: A woodsman toiled among the trees and trudged along slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbering is both the timber trade and a heavy, clumsy way of walking, two unrelated senses of one verb.

clue.text: I turned out to be devoid of proven ability

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone admits they proved to have no demonstrated talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' reads as a phrase, but 'out' is the anagram signal on I TURNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Untried means not yet tested, so any ability has not been shown.

clue.text: Blooming lovely is that bit of fighter's kit!

parts.note: the words BLOOMIN and LY surround the letters G LOVE, so the phrase is boxing that glove

explanation.surface: A cheerful cockney exclamation about a piece of boxing equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: GLOVE sits in a box inside 'Blooming lovely'.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing glove is the padded mitt a boxer wears, standard equipment in the ring.

clue.text: One has such a car? It brings ruin!

parts.note: the word ruin is RUN wrapped around I, and the clue's It (One) is that I, so the answer read as an instruction builds it

explanation.surface: A warning that owning a certain car leads to financial disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as wordplay, RUN AROUND I (One), and it builds RUIN. 'It brings' tells you the answer produces the clue word.
explanation.definitionFit: A runaround, like a runabout, is a small car used for short trips.

clue.text: This writer's in stupid short trousers

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other
short says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: stupid means dense
the writer means me, so this writer's is I'm

explanation.surface: The author confesses to wearing silly shorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like it describes the trousers, but it is the cue to drop the last letter of the word for stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: Denims are jeans or trousers made of the hard-wearing cotton fabric denim.

clue.text: Religious writings penned by wise man, an English poet

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, as in a pen

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
AV is the Authorized Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: Scripture written down by a sage who was also an English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Savage was an eighteenth-century English poet, friend of Samuel Johnson.

clue.text: Hasten to border, finally changing direction

indicators.note: changing tells us these letters are altered into a fresh order
finally picks only the closing letter of the word border

explanation.surface: An instruction to rush to the frontier, then switch course at the last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes R from border; 'changing' rearranges HASTENTO plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: Northeast is a compass bearing, a point midway between north and east, so it is a direction.

clue.text: No one getting cross, rolling round? I sure don't react!

indicators.note: rolling round suggests turning over, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: no one means NONE
a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: Nobody gets angry or turns around, and a calm voice declares itself unreactive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling round' reverses NONE + X. The definition is the gas speaking: xenon is a noble gas, famously reluctant to form compounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenon is one of the noble gases, chemically inert elements that hardly ever combine with anything.

clue.text: Advance booking in doubt

definitions.meaning: a table or seat booked ahead
having ... means having doubts or misgivings

explanation.surface: Someone books in advance but still feels uncertain.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservation is both a booked place and a qualm, two distinct dictionary senses of the same noun.

clue.text: Revived or new form of green energy getting assessed

indicators.note: a new form means the word is reshaped into a different order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
assessed means rated

explanation.surface: A renewed type of green power being evaluated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new form of' rearranges GREEN to REGEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To regenerate is to bring back to life or vigour, so regenerated means revived.

clue.text: Gossip, having poured out our drink

indicators.note: poured out says the following word is emptied from the longer one

parts.note: gossip means rumour

explanation.surface: Someone who has been gossiping has spilt everyone's drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having poured out' removes OUR from RUMOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane, an example of an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Endless danger? Gosh — it's where something is as close as possible!

definitions.text: where something is as close as possible

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: danger means peril
gee is an exclamation of surprise like gosh

explanation.surface: An excited remark about danger and something coming as near as it can.
explanation.definitionFit: Perigee is the point in an orbit, as of the Moon, nearest to Earth, the closest approach.

clue.text: Way factory gives reason for stop-go procedure

parts.note: a way is a road
a works is a factory

explanation.surface: A factory explains why it works in fits and starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Repairs to a road usually bring temporary traffic lights, so drivers alternately stop and go.

clue.text: Canoe extracted by archaeologist?

definitions.meaning: a canoe made by hollowing out a tree trunk
an archaeologist's finds are ... of the ground

explanation.surface: An ancient boat that a digger has unearthed.
explanation.definitionFit: A dugout is a hollowed log boat, and finds an archaeologist excavates are literally dug from the earth.

clue.text: Papa not polite and nice, not one for discretion

parts.note: Papa is P in the NATO alphabet
not polite means rude

indicators.note: not one says the letter standing for one is dropped from the word

explanation.surface: Father is impolite and pleasant, but no fan of tact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not one' drops I (the Roman one) from NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudence is careful good judgment, the quality of acting with discretion.

clue.text: Like some music of Queen in recording

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: CD is a compact disc, a recording
Anne was Queen of Great Britain

explanation.surface: A description of a royal's music found on a record.
explanation.definitionFit: Canned music is recorded rather than live, often piped into shops and lifts.

clue.text: Poker-faced cleric hugging a daughter quietly

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping round, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A stony-faced churchman quietly embraces his child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quietly' is P, the musical piano; all three short pieces sit inside the cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadpan means showing no expression, the blank face a poker player keeps.

clue.text: One who criticises son, getting less affectionate

parts.note: less affectionate means colder

explanation.surface: A parent who nags their boy finds him growing cooler towards them.
explanation.definitionFit: A scolder is a person who rebukes or nags, the agent noun of scold.

clue.text: Join in urgent message to expose pathetic people

indicators.note: in puts the first piece inside the second

parts.note: SOS is the distress call
to add is to join on

explanation.surface: Signing up to an emergency alert that unmasks feeble people.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddo is British slang for a dull or pitiable person, a loser.

clue.text: Vice around university? Say not a word

indicators.note: around means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a vice is a clamp, the workshop tool

explanation.surface: Corruption on campus that nobody will talk about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vice' suggests wickedness; it is the gripping tool.
explanation.definitionFit: To clam up is an idiom for refusing to speak, shutting tight like a clam.

clue.text: Act like any would, when just starting out

indicators.note: just starting out points to the opening letter of each of the words

explanation.surface: Behave as anyone would when they are new to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act' looks like a verb, but it is the noun, an Act of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: An Act passed by a legislature becomes a law, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Looked again at study needing to get tidied up

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
dressed can mean arranged neatly, as a shop window is dressed

explanation.surface: A room for study needed sorting out before reconsideration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' looks like a room but is the verb read.
explanation.definitionFit: To readdress a problem is to tackle or examine it once more.

clue.text: Hasty author

explanation.definitionFit: Swift is an adjective for speed and the surname of the Irish satirist Jonathan Swift.

clue.text: Revolutionary army returning to wreck

parts.note: to wreck or spoil is to mar

indicators.note: returning means the letters go back the other way

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the UK reserve force

explanation.surface: Insurgent troops head back to destroy something.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul Marat was a radical leader of the French Revolution, stabbed in his bath.

clue.text: Member's movement perhaps supporting country

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a country is a nation

explanation.surface: A political wing's campaign that backs the state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' and 'movement' suggest politics; here a member is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronation is the inward rotation of a hand or foot, a motion of a limb.

clue.text: Always giving a positive response

definitions.meaning: an old and Scots word for ever or always

explanation.surface: Someone who forever says yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Aye means yes in voting and dialect, and in poetry it also means forever.

clue.text: The old man meeting unhappy woman in US city

parts.note: old man is slang for father, pa
unhappy means sad
Ena is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Father meets a miserable woman in an American town.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasadena is a city in Los Angeles County, California, known for the Rose Parade.

clue.text: Report of e.g. copper's courage

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: copper is an example of a metal

explanation.surface: An account of a police officer's bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a police officer, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mettle is spirit and resilience in the face of difficulty, a synonym of bravery.
